paper_title: Stochastic Deep Supervision for Gallery-Consistent Early-Exit Face Recognition

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Vision Transformers (ViTs) perform strongly in face recognition (FR), yet their fixed-depth inference limits deployment in resource-constrained settings. We propose SD-ViT, a training framework that gives a usable exit at every block depth by making every depth produce discriminative embeddings, for budget-selected fixed-depth exits. Standard ViTs supervise intermediate layers only through backpropagation, so their intermediate representations are not directly optimized to form usable identity embeddings. SD-ViT adds a stochastic auxiliary signal: at each iteration a randomly selected intermediate block is passed through the same embedding head as the final layer and trained with a weighted margin-penalty softmax loss. The objective is thus stochastically sampled deep supervision through a shared classifier. Because both loss terms share that head and classifier, intermediate tokens are trained to map into the same embedding space as final-layer tokens. This matters for FR, where matching is by similarity: a probe processed at an early exit can be compared directly against full-depth gallery embeddings, with no gallery recomputation or adaptation layers. On established benchmarks, SD-ViT stays within 0.4 IJB-C points of the same backbone trained conventionally at full depth, while its early-exit probes recover over 96% of their own full-depth performance at 50% of the computational cost without modifying the reference gallery. A single verification threshold calibrated at full depth remains usable from quarter depth onward.

Code: https://github.com/gurayozgur/SD-ViT. 1. Introduction FR accuracy is driven by deep networks [22] trained with margin-based softmax objectives [14, 27, 47], and increasingly by ViTs [17], which surpass convolutional backbones on FR benchmarks [13, 30, 31]. ViT processes every input through fixed stack of blocks at the same cost regardless of input difficulty or device budget, which is at odds with deployment: one model must run from edge processors to datacenter accelerators under budgets differing by orders of magnitude [15]. Compact architectures [5, 10, 51], compression [7] and distillation [23, 28, 33] each yield another static model from separate run, so covering several budgets means training, storing and switching whole networks. Early-exit networks are the flexible alternative: one model with intermediate classifiers, so inference stops shallow for easy inputs or tight budgets [25, 46]. They were built for closed-set classification, where each exit has its own classifier over fixed label set and the exits need not share representation [25, 29, 46]. FR does not fit that template: it is open-set, matching probe to gallery of enrolled embeddings by cosine similarity, so independent per-exit heads produce incompatible spaces and shallow embedding cannot match full-depth gallery. The closed-set and distillation analogues, per-exit heads that would require re-embedding the gallery at every depth [3] and learned adaptation layers between depths [41], are unattractive here. Galleries can be massive, distributed or privacy-constrained, and adaptation layers break the singleembedding-space assumption enrollment pipelines rely on. Early-exit FR therefore requires that every depth emit embeddings in one shared space, compatible with gallery enrolled once at full depth. We address this with Stochastic Deep-supervision for ViTs (SD-ViT), shared-classifier form of deep supervision  (Fig. 1)  . At each iteration, besides the full-depth output, SD-ViT reads out one auxiliary embedding at uniformly sampled intermediate block, decodes it with the same head, and scores it against the same prototypes under the same margin-penalty loss. The shared head maps tokens from every depth into one embedding space, and the shared prototypes give each identity single center in it. Deep supervision is long established [32, 45]. What distinguishes SD-ViT is not that intermediate depths are supervised but through what: the final exits own head and classifier instead of exit-specific ones, which makes the embeddings interchangeable across depth. Our controls show that the sampled exit must be trained by the margin loss itself, not by feature matching (Sec. 4.3). At inference probe Figure 1. At each iteration secondary exit is read out at uniformly sampled block z(k), U{1, . . . , 1}. Both are decoded by the same head and scored against the same prototypes under margin-penalty loss, combined with weight ω (Eq. 4). Sharing and across depths places all embeddings in one space, so at inference probe may exit at any depth (Eq. 5) and match gallery enrolled once at full depth. may exit at any depth and match full-depth gallery by plain cosine similarity. Sampling different block each step spreads supervision uniformly over depth, so every block depth becomes usable exit after one training run. Sampling is single-sample estimator of supervising all exits, and Sec. 4.3 finds it on par with deterministic all-exit supervision at one seventh of the auxiliary cost. We contribute: (i) the identification of gallery consistency, one shared embedding space across depths, as the central obstacle to earlyexit FR, (ii) SD-ViT, in which uniformly sampled auxiliary exit shares the final layers head and prototypes, making every depth gallery-compatible with no teacher and no adaptation layers, and (iii) evidence that one training run yields usable exit at every block depth, with full-depth accuracy within 0.4 IJB-C points of conventional training, no gallery recomputation, and single verification threshold usable from quarter depth onward. 2. Related Work Deep supervision and knowledge distillation. Deeplysupervised nets [32] and GoogLeNet [45] add auxiliary losses at intermediate layers to aid optimisation and discard the auxiliary heads after training. Knowledge distillation [23] transfers from teacher to student via soft-label or feature-matching objectives, and born-again networks [20] and deep mutual learning [53] remove the fixed teacher. For FR it has used triplet [19], rank-based [28], angular [44] and reverse-feature [33] objectives, and AdaDistill [9] injects teacher-derived class centers into the student margin loss. BYOT [52] combines the two: it attaches auxiliary classifiers to intermediate CNN sections and distills from the deepest into the shallower ones. SD-ViT differs from both lines. Its auxiliary exit is not discarded after training but deployed as an early exit, and it is decoded by the final exits own head and scored against the same prototypes instead of separate classifier. It uses no teacher and no adaptation layers, and couples the exits solely through this shared head and prototypes. Identity objectives for FR. Margin-penalty softmax losses [6, 14, 30, 47] and auxiliary objectives [21, 48] separate identities and compact each around its center, but only for the final-layer embedding. SD-ViT applies such supervision at sampled intermediate depth as well, against the prototypes that define the final space. Early-exit and budget-selected inference. Early-exit networks add intermediate classifiers so that easy inputs terminate early [25, 29, 46, 56]. LayerSkip [18] is the closit trains lanest precedent for our parameter sharing: guage model with layer dropout [24] and an early-exit loss through shared output head, so intermediate layers be2 come decodable without per-layer heads. Among early-exit ViTs, LGViT [50] uses heterogeneous local-global heads and EnViT [16] exit-aware dropout, both trained by selfdistillation. All target closed-set classification, where the label set ties the exits together and nothing forces their representations to be comparable. Open-set FR adds that requirement. Token pruning and merging [4, 39] reduce the cost of each block, not the number of blocks, so they are orthogonal to SD-ViT and could be combined with it. Closest to our setting, ViT-FREE [12] performs training-free early exiting in pretrained ViT-FR models, exploiting constant token dimensionality with synthetic-data adaptation step, and EX-FIQA [38] fuses intermediate representations for quality assessment. SD-ViT shares the observation that ViT keeps one dimensionality at every depth, but instead of reading exits from fixed backbone post-hoc it optimizes every block to produce gallery-consistent embeddings. We compare against both of its settings (Sec. 4.2). Trainingfree ViT-FREE is precisely our Baseline read-out. ViTFREEF trains an exit-specific projection and prototype set per depth. We report it under self-evaluation, the setting it was designed for, and under our gallery-fixed setting. ViTs for FR. TransFace [13] addresses ViT overfitting with patch-level augmentation and hard-sample mining, Part-fViT [43] adds landmark-driven part tokens, and KP-RPE [31] replaces learnable positional encodings with keypoint-relative ones. All treat the ViT as fixed-depth backbone for single full-depth pass, addressing neither multi-exit inference nor gallery-consistent retrieval. SDViT adds stochastic shared-classifier deep-supervision objective that makes every block produce gallery-compatible embeddings, with no change to the inference architecture. 3.
